name: Ko-Li Bar
notes: Kakigori/Japanese shaved-ice dessert bar. Own sites (sandiegoyakyudori.com/page/ko-li and ko-li.com) have no menu or price page at all -- only location/hours and seasonal-flavor announcement posts with no prices. No DoorDash/UberEats/Grubhub listing found via search. Yelp business page and menu tab return 403/CAPTCHA to curl and r.jina.ai; Yelp photo gallery loaded only 35 of ~1229 photos in the in-app browser pane (infinite-scroll would not trigger) and none of those had a menu-board photo, so I could not locate a dated priced photo either. Reviews mention prices around $16/item but that is an unverified summary, not a read price. Blocking rather than not_found since this is clearly a real, priced dessert menu that a Chrome-equipped pass with more scroll time could likely capture from Yelp photos.
blocked: no reachable priced source (own site has no menu; Yelp 403s curl; browser photo gallery pagination did not surface a menu-board photo in the time available)

name: Diamond Doughnuts
notes: No working first-party site (diamond-donuts.res-menu.net and .com both return an empty body/blank shell even in-browser; findmenuworld.com is a dead 'Index of /' listing). Not found on DoorDash search. Used a dated Yelp photo of the shop's own in-store price board, captioned 'Great price.', dated August 2025 (about a year old, the most recent priced photo in the gallery of 41 -- an older March 2016 board photo and a December 2017 review caption both show markedly lower cents-level prices from a different era and were NOT used, per the no-blending-eras rule). Read via zoomed crops of the full-resolution photo. Only rows that showed an actual price on the board are included; items listed with no price tile (Devils Food, Choco Raised, Sugar, Cream Cheese, Apple Fritter, Bear Claw, Cinnamon Rolls, Cinnamon Twist, Low Fat Milk, Choco Milk, Quik Choco, Quik Strawberry) were dropped rather than guessed. A separate 'Egg, Cheese and...' breakfast-sandwich poster on the wall had no visible price in this photo, so breakfast sandwiches are not included (an older 2016 photo showed ~$3.29-$3.79 for these but that price is stale and was not used). Board prices are in cents (e.g. 165¢) and were converted to dollars.

name: Heytea
notes: Own site (heytea.com) is a bare client-rendered React SPA shell with no server-side content to curl, and the WeChat-style delivery aggregator fantuanorder.com sits behind a slide-to-verify CAPTCHA (not attempted, per rules). Captured full priced menu from the Uber Eats storefront for this exact address (12925 El Camino Real, San Diego, CA 92130) via the in-app browser pane; delivery was showing unavailable but the full priced menu (pickup) rendered. The store's own subtitle reads '圣地亚哥Del Mar店-三方外卖' ("San Diego Del Mar store - third-party delivery"), flagging this as a delivery-channel menu, so I ran the markup test: prices end in odd cents (.49/.99/.68/.98/.88, e.g. $10.49, $8.49, $5.49) with no items landing on round or .95 values, and dividing by 1.04/1.1/1.15/1.2 does not produce a cleaner distribution -- this looks like Heytea's normal U.S. psychological pricing, not a markup, so I kept it at medium confidence (tier-3 delivery storefront) rather than blocking it. Could not reach DoorDash (no SD-area listing found) or Heytea's own ordering channel to cross-check. Dropped the 'Staff Picks' and duplicate 'In Season'/'tennis season edition' carousel entries where the same item also appeared under its real category at the same price, keeping one row per unique item/size.

name: Jorge's Mexicatessen
notes: Batch website (jorgesmexicatessengo.site) does not resolve (DNS failure). Found the real own site via search: eatjorgesmexicatessen.com, address 417 Santa Fe Dr, Encinitas -- confirms identity/branch and the full dish-name/section list, but it is a Durable website-builder page whose menu block carries an empty \"price\" field on every single item (genuinely unpriced on the restaurant's own site). Captured full priced menu instead from the DoorDash storefront for the same address, which explicitly states 'Prices on this menu are set directly by the Merchant.' The DoorDash JSON-LD block alone only exposed 8 of 17 categories (91 items, matching the known JSON-LD-is-incomplete failure mode) -- I instead parsed the page's escaped RSC flight payload for 'MenuPageItem' objects and matched each to its 'category_id' logging field, recovering 14 of 17 categories (139 unique items) whose per-category counts matched the store's own MenuBookCategory totals exactly. Two categories were absent from the payload entirely even after scrolling and are left unread rather than guessed: 'PREP FOOD' (10 items) and an oddly-named, unlabeled category called 'No' (17 items) -- neither is included here. Dropped the duplicate 'Most Ordered' carousel (12 items, all also present under their real category at the same price). No markup pattern found (prices end in a wide mix of .90/.95/.30/.25/.85/.65/.00/.09 etc, not a clean division of round numbers), consistent with the page's own 'set by the Merchant' disclaimer, so kept at medium (tier-3 delivery storefront) rather than high or blocked.

name: Jomaru Korean Hot Pot
notes: Batch website (jomaruusa.com) 403s a plain curl and its /menu path resolves to the site's own 'error page' (오류안내 페이지) -- confirmed as a genuine server-side block rather than a JS-rendering issue. Found the restaurant's real first-party ordering platform via search: jomaru.menu11.com/sandiego/order, plain server-rendered HTML, no browser needed. Address on the page (4681 Convoy Street Suite D, San Diego CA 92111) matches the batch address exactly. Captured all 5 menu categories shown (Appetizer, Main Dish, Specialty, Drinks, Extra) -- this is a gamjatang/Korean-hotpot specialist so Main Dish (bone soups) and Specialty (BBQ/rice/noodle dishes) being the bulk of the menu is the expected shape. All prices are round dollar amounts with no odd cents to test for a markup, and this is the restaurant's own first-party platform, so kept at high confidence. Two items had stray rendering artifacts in the raw text (an extra '2' after 'Kimchi Gam-Ja-Tang L' and a doubled open-paren before 'Pork Cutlet') which were cleaned up as obvious formatting noise, not price changes.

name: Mesa Agricola
notes: Own site (mesaagricola.com) is Squarespace with no priced core menu -- its only priced items are a small 'Catering pickup' product list (Whole Basque Cheesecake $95, Build-your-own tacos 12ct $60, Prepared burritos 1/2 dozen $54, Cookies 1/2 dozen $30, Pint of Guisado $42, Pint of Beans/Rice $13.50 each, Corn/Flour Tortillas 1/2 dozen $9-$12), which is a catering adjunct, not the real per-item tacos & burritos menu, so it was NOT used. The real ordering platform, linked from the homepage, is mesaagricola.square.site (Square Online). Its HTML shell is empty of item data to a plain curl (confirmed: no catalog JSON server-rendered, only fee/tip config). Opened it in-browser instead: the storefront shows 'Sorry, we're closed. We aren't accepting online orders at the moment. There are no pickup items available at the selected location.' Posted hours are Wednesday-Sunday 11AM-6PM; today is Monday, so the restaurant is closed on its normal schedule and Square Online appears to hide its whole catalog behind the closed-store gate rather than exposing it in a REST/RSC payload the way Clover or order.online do (no window-level catalog state and no readable GET catalog endpoint found). This is a same-day closed-store gate, not a missing menu, so blocking rather than not_found -- retry on a Wednesday-Sunday.
